newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Selective buying boosts Singapore shares at close.
newsitem.headline: Selective buying boosts Singapore shares at close.

text.p: Selective buying of blue chips and under-valued stocks boosted the Singapore stock market to a stronger close on Wednesday.
"Investors took the opportunity to buy stocks which have fallen sharply recently and are also accumulating blue chips," said a local broker.
The Straits Times Industrials Index rebounded above the 2,000 level to end at 2,004.26, up 14.06 points.
The property index ended 5.08 points up at 652.04, led by Cycle & Carriage, which rose S$0.40 to S$14.80 and CityDev which rose S$0.20 to S$11.70 as fears of more property curbs faded.
Foreign tranches of blue chips like SIA, OCBC, DBS and UOB also rose.
Singapore Telecommunications rose S$0.07 on renewed institution interest to end at S$2.44 in active trade of more than 6.1 million shares.
Property company United Industrial Corp, which was also active with more than 5.6 million shares traded, ended unchanged at S$1.09.
Total market volume was a moderate 109 million shares, with 262 gainers and 71 losers.
